title: hpc
text: The hpc subcommand configures Linux HPC environments.

title: hpc
text:
Commands
hpc
hpc scratch
hpc apptainer
hpc slurm
hpc git
hpc r [--not-radian] [--not-lintr] [--switch-r]

title: hpc
text:
Installation
Install setupmjr using the supported method for the HPC host. For a no-sudo Linux installation, use the user-local release installer described in Installation. Confirm the result with:
setupmjr --version

title: hpc
text:
Master setup
setupmjr hpc
The master command is Linux-only and stops on the first failed setup step. It runs this sequence:

Configure Bash rc.d, executable paths and login/profile integration.
Configure Zsh rc.d, executable paths and login/profile integration.
Configure Git and GitHub authentication.
Install the HPC scratch configuration.
Install the Apptainer helpers.
Install the SLURM helpers.
Configure R with the normal setupmjr r defaults.

In practical terms, setupmjr hpc does the following:

Helps store large files effectively: Large files are stored in /scratch when available rather than /home, to respect HPC storage policies.
Authenticates with Git: GitHub authentication uses either an existing persistent gh login or one protected setupmjr-managed token file for headless/HPC environments.
Adds Apptainer and SLURM helpers: Helper scripts are installed under ~/.local/bin.
Configures R: The normal setupmjr r defaults configure radian and lintr.

Each feature can also be configured independently with the subcommands below.

Git
setupmjr hpc git
This calls the normal setupmjr git setup. Authentication is suitable for headless HPC use:

if gh auth login has already established durable GitHub CLI authentication, Git is configured with gh auth setup-git;
otherwise setupmjr stores one GitHub token under ~/.config/setupmjr/auth/github.token, with private permissions, and configures Git to read it through the standard credential-helper interface.

The token itself is not embedded in shell startup files or Git configuration. Existing active GH_TOKEN= assignments left by older setupmjr versions are removed from setupmjr’s login.sh files during migration.
This credential-helper design is also intended to work with R gitcreds and with VS Code Dev Containers’ Git credential forwarding. In a Remote SSH -> HPC -> Dev Container workflow, configure authentication on the HPC host first. If a particular Dev Container still fails to reuse the host helper, treat that as a forwarding problem rather than copying a PAT into the repository or container definition.
See Git for the full authentication model and fallback details.


Scratch space
setupmjr hpc scratch
HPCs commonly provide /scratch/$USER for large files and caches. This command installs ~/.bashrc.d/hpc-scratch.sh, which configures scratch-backed locations for Apptainer/Singularity images and R library/renv caches.
The master setupmjr hpc command wires Bash rc.d before installing this file. The standalone hpc scratch command only installs the file, so run setupmjr shell bash rc.d first if Bash is not already sourcing ~/.bashrc.d.


SLURM
setupmjr hpc slurm
This installs SLURM helper scripts into ~/.local/bin, including:

slurm-sbatch for submitting a job and recording submission details;
slurm-sintx for starting an interactive session;
slurm-squeue for listing the current user’s jobs.



Apptainer
setupmjr hpc apptainer
This installs the embedded apptainer-* helper scripts into ~/.local/bin, excluding apptainer-vscode.


R
setupmjr hpc r
This calls the normal R setup and accepts the same flags:
setupmjr hpc r --not-lintr
setupmjr hpc r --switch-r
See R for the flag behaviour.

title: repo
text: The repo subcommand configures the current repository.

title: repo
text:
Commands
repo readme
repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]
repo action <action-name>

title: repo
text:
repo readme
This command interactively scaffolds a standard README.md with a title, purpose, contacts, links and details sections.
setupmjr repo readme

title: repo
text:
repo devcontainer
Copy a reference .devcontainer configuration into the current repository:
setupmjr repo devcontainer
setupmjr repo devcontainer --repo MiguelRodo/comp@main

--repo selects the source repository and branch in <owner>/<repo>@<branch> form. The default is MiguelRodo/comp@main.
--build also installs the prebuild-devcontainer.yml workflow example from the latest published MiguelRodo/actions release.

The source archive is fully staged before extraction, so a timeout or interrupted response cannot feed a partial archive into tar. Repository and branch values are passed as command arguments rather than interpolated into a shell command.
setupmjr-owned HTTP downloads use a finite request timeout, preserve URL/status context on failures, and only replace destination files after complete writes.

title: repo
text:
Install repos
Repository orchestration belongs to the standalone repos command. Install or update it with:
setupmjr install --repos
Then invoke repos directly. The release archive is staged in a temporary directory and is not extracted after a failed or incomplete download.

title: repo
text:
repo action
Install a workflow example published by the canonical MiguelRodo/actions repository:
setupmjr repo action <action-name>
setupmjr resolves the latest published actions release, then downloads examples/<action-name>.yml from that exact release tag into .github/workflows/. It keeps no embedded workflow copies and does not fall back to mutable actions/main.
Use the example filename from the latest published MiguelRodo/actions release without the .yml suffix. If that example is not present in the release, the command fails rather than installing a local or development copy.
Workflow downloads are staged in .github/workflows/ and replace the final path only after the response completes successfully. Errors include the requested action name, resolved release tag and HTTP status where available.

title: r
text: The r subcommand configures R-related user and project files.

title: r
text:
Command
r [--not-radian] [--not-lintr] [--switch-r]
Running:
setupmjr r
configures the user-level radian and lintr defaults.

Flags

--not-radian skips the ~/.radian_profile configuration.
--not-lintr skips the ~/.lintr configuration.
--switch-r adds the project-local scripts/r/switch_r.R helper and ensures the current repository’s .Rprofile sources it.

For example:
setupmjr r --not-lintr
setupmjr r --switch-r
The HPC wrapper accepts the same R flags, for example:
setupmjr hpc r --not-lintr

title: r
text:
Details
Unless --not-radian is supplied, setupmjr ensures ~/.radian_profile contains:
options(radian.auto_match = FALSE)
Unless --not-lintr is supplied, setupmjr ensures ~/.lintr contains:
linters: linters_with_defaults(
    object_length_linter = NULL,
    object_name_linter = NULL)
With --switch-r, setupmjr creates scripts/r/switch_r.R if it is absent and places this source line at the top of the current repository’s .Rprofile:
try(source("scripts/r/switch_r.R"))

title: shell
text: The shell subcommand configures Bash or Zsh startup files. setupmjr bash is shorthand for setupmjr shell bash.

title: shell
text:
Commands
shell <shell> rc.d
shell <shell> path
shell <shell> login [--not-profile]

bash rc.d
bash path
bash login [--not-profile]

title: shell
text:
rc.d
setupmjr shell bash rc.d
setupmjr shell zsh rc.d
This ensures ~/.<shell>rc.d exists and configures ~/.<shell>rc to source readable files from that directory.

title: shell
text:
Details
The sourcing loop is:
for i in $HOME/.<shell>rc.d/*; do [ -r "$i" ] && source "$i"; done

title: shell
text:
path
setupmjr shell bash path
setupmjr shell zsh path
This first ensures the shell’s rc.d directory is wired in, then installs path-executables.sh there so ~/bin and ~/.local/bin are available on PATH without duplicating entries.

title: shell
text:
login
setupmjr shell bash login
setupmjr shell zsh login
This installs login.sh in the shell’s rc.d directory and configures the corresponding login profile to source the directory. Bash uses ~/.profile unless ~/.bash_profile already exists; Zsh uses ~/.zprofile.
Use --not-profile when you want the login.sh file but do not want setupmjr to modify the login profile:
setupmjr shell bash login --not-profile

title: Installation
text: setupmjr is distributed as a compiled Go CLI binary. The canonical installation paths are the published APT repository, the release installer scripts, Scoop on Windows, or a Go source build.

title: Installation
text:
Ubuntu / Debian

APT repository
Configure the published apt-miguelrodo repository once:
sudo apt-get install -y curl gpg
curl -fsSL https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo/KEY.gpg \
  | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg] https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo stable main" \
  | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/apt-miguelrodo.list >/dev/null
sudo apt-get update
Then install or upgrade normally:
sudo apt-get install -y setupmjr
The Debian package depends on bash and repos, so APT installs those dependencies through the repository as needed.


User-local release installer
For a no-sudo installation, clone the repository and run the release installer:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
bash install-local.sh
The script downloads the latest release binary, verifies its checksum when checksums.txt and a SHA-256 tool are available, and installs it into the first writable directory already on PATH. If none is writable, it falls back to ~/.local/bin and prints the required PATH instruction. If repos is not already available, the installed setupmjr binary runs setupmjr install --repos.
To uninstall an installation recorded by the local installer:
bash uninstall-local.sh

title: Installation
text:
macOS
Use the same user-local release installer:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
bash install-local.sh
The installer supports both amd64 and arm64 release binaries and falls back to ~/.local/bin when no writable PATH directory is available.

title: Installation
text:
Windows

Scoop
A current Scoop manifest is published in MiguelRodo/scoop-bucket:
scoop bucket add MiguelRodo https://github.com/MiguelRodo/scoop-bucket
scoop install setupmjr
The manifest declares repos as a dependency.


Installer script
Alternatively, clone the repository and run the PowerShell installer:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
.\install.ps1
The script downloads the latest release binary into the first writable directory already on Path. If repos is not already available, the installed setupmjr binary runs setupmjr install --repos and the installer fails if that dependency installation fails.
To uninstall the recorded installation:
.\install.ps1 -Uninstall

title: Installation
text:
From source
With Go installed, install directly from the module path:
go install github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/cmd/setupmjr@latest
Or build a local clone:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
go build -o setupmjr ./cmd/setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
Managed components
After installing setupmjr, use its top-level install command for the external tools whose installation glue it owns:
setupmjr install --repos
setupmjr install --pj
setupmjr install --gh-skill
Flags may be combined. Installers run in a fixed order and stop at the first error:
setupmjr install --repos --pj --gh-skill

--repos installs the latest released MiguelRodo/repos binary into ~/.local/bin. Run repos directly afterwards.
--pj installs or updates pj from MiguelRodo/pj by shallow-cloning the floating v0 tag and running its installer.
--gh-skill installs github-projects from MiguelRodo/github-projects-skill for universal agents at user scope, pinned to main.

At least one target flag is required.

title: Installation
Installation
text:
Verify installation
setupmjr --version
setupmjr --help

title: agent
text: Use the agent command for user-level coding-agent configuration. Provider setup belongs here; pj only launches already-configured agents.

title: agent
text:
Inspect agent configuration
Show the effective Codex provider, Copilot provider and configured opt-in subagent:
setupmjr agent --config
List the available choices and short aliases:
setupmjr agent --list
Running setupmjr agent without options prints command help.

title: agent
text:
Configure model-provider authentication
Store the DeepSeek API credential without changing any agent’s active provider:
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek
# short form
setupmjr agent -a d
The command reuses DEEPSEEK_API_KEY when it is already set, then checks the managed DeepSeek credential and existing Codex DeepSeek configurations. If no key is available, it prompts for one without echoing it.
The reusable key is stored at:
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/auth/deepseek.key
with private permissions. The credential can be reused by both the Codex and Copilot DeepSeek configurations.
Crucially, --auth is credential-only. It does not set COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE, COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL, COPILOT_MODEL, or any other provider-selection variable, and it does not change the current Codex or Copilot provider.
At present deepseek is the only managed --auth endpoint. The endpoint argument is explicit so additional credentials can be added without changing the command shape.

title: agent
text:
Switch the Copilot provider
GitHub-managed Copilot models are the default value for -p, so these are equivalent:
setupmjr agent -p
setupmjr agent -p g
setupmjr agent --copilot-provider github
Switch Copilot to DeepSeek:
setupmjr agent -p d
setupmjr agent --copilot-provider deepseek
DeepSeek provider selection requires the credential to have been stored first with:
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek
When DeepSeek is selected, setupmjr writes the managed Copilot environment at:
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/copilot.env
and sources it from Bash and Zsh startup files. The active DeepSeek configuration is:
COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic
COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=https://api.deepseek.com/anthropic
COPILOT_MODEL=deepseek-flash
COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS=840000
COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=128000
Here, COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic selects the Anthropic-compatible wire protocol used to communicate with DeepSeek’s endpoint. It does not select Anthropic as the model vendor.
The raw DeepSeek key is not copied into the provider environment. The environment reads the private credential file only when DeepSeek is the active Copilot provider.
Switching back to github writes an environment that unsets the BYOK provider variables, restoring GitHub-managed Copilot model selection in new shells. Restart the shell, or source ~/.config/setupmjr/agent/copilot.env, after switching.
DeepSeek BYOK does not itself sign Copilot into GitHub. GitHub authentication remains separate and can coexist with either provider choice.

title: agent
text:
Switch the primary Codex provider
OpenAI/ChatGPT is the default value for -c, so these are equivalent:
setupmjr agent -c
setupmjr agent -c o
setupmjr agent --codex-provider openai
Switch Codex to DeepSeek:
setupmjr agent -c d
setupmjr agent --codex-provider deepseek
The first DeepSeek setup uses DeepSeek’s official Codex setup script and selects the Flash model. setupmjr reads DEEPSEEK_API_KEY when it is set, reuses a key from an existing managed DeepSeek configuration when possible, or prompts for the key without echoing it.
The script is downloaded over HTTPS with setupmjr’s bounded downloader into a temporary directory before it is run. A timeout, non-success HTTP response or incomplete download prevents execution. The script runs with bash --noprofile --norc and a reduced environment containing the target Codex home, the DeepSeek key when required, and ordinary process values such as PATH; unrelated environment credentials are not forwarded.
This remains a remote-code trust boundary. DeepSeek’s current Codex integration publishes the one-click installer at a mutable CDN URL and does not provide a versioned script or checksum for setupmjr to pin. setupmjr therefore does not invent a brittle hash or vendor DeepSeek’s large model catalogue. If you do not want to execute the vendor script, use DeepSeek’s documented manual Codex configuration instead: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/agent_integrations/codex/.
Before changing provider, setupmjr stores private snapshots of the active Codex config.toml and models.json under:
~/.config/setupmjr/agent/codex/
After both providers have been seen once, -c d and -c o switch by restoring those snapshots rather than rerunning the full DeepSeek installer.
If DeepSeek was already installed manually with the official setup script before setupmjr started managing providers, the first switch back to OpenAI uses DeepSeek’s official restore path once and then records the restored OpenAI state. Later switches are local snapshot restores.
Provider changes affect the ordinary Codex home at ~/.codex, so they apply to Codex clients that share that configuration. Restart active Codex clients after switching. A DeepSeek session may have logged Codex out of ChatGPT, so restoring the OpenAI configuration does not guarantee that the ChatGPT account is still authenticated.
The automated DeepSeek bootstrap requires Bash and is intended for Linux, macOS and WSL environments. It no longer requires curl.

title: agent
text:
Configure an opt-in subagent
agy is the default value for -s:
setupmjr agent -s
setupmjr agent -s agy
setupmjr agent --subagent agy
This installs the bounded Codex guidance and narrow execution rule for delegating explicitly authorised work to Gemini through agy. Existing Codex instructions outside the managed block are preserved.
To use DeepSeek instead:
setupmjr agent -s deepseek
The DeepSeek subagent uses an isolated Codex home:
~/.codex-deepseek-subagent
It does not change the primary Codex provider. The managed guidance invokes the worker with codex exec --sandbox workspace-write and the isolated CODEX_HOME. As with agy, delegation remains opt-in: Codex may use the subagent only when you explicitly authorise it for the current task or conversation.
Selecting one subagent replaces the managed configuration for the other. --subagent-agy remains as a deprecated compatibility alias for --subagent agy.

title: agent
text:
Credential storage
setupmjr agent --auth deepseek stores the reusable DeepSeek API key in ~/.config/setupmjr/agent/auth/deepseek.key with private permissions. Authentication alone does not alter provider selection. When Copilot is explicitly switched to DeepSeek, its managed environment reads that file rather than embedding the raw key in .bashrc, .zshrc, or the provider environment.
DeepSeek’s official Codex format also stores the API key in config.toml. The saved DeepSeek provider snapshot therefore contains that key as well. setupmjr creates its provider-state directories with mode 0700 and writes credential and snapshot files with mode 0600. Treat these files as credentials and do not commit or share them.

title: git
text: The git subcommand configures Git identity and authentication.

title: git
text:
Commands
git
git profile
git auth [text|cache|mngr] [--system|--local] [--remove]

title: git
text:
Git setup
setupmjr git
This configures your Git name/email when they are missing and then configures GitHub authentication.
setupmjr git auth chooses between two durable authentication paths:

If gh has a persistent login for github.com, setupmjr runs gh auth setup-git --hostname github.com and lets GitHub CLI own the credential.
Otherwise, setupmjr uses its headless/HPC fallback and stores one token at ~/.config/setupmjr/auth/github.token.

The GitHub CLI check deliberately ignores GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN, so an environment-only token is not mistaken for a durable gh auth login.

Scope and replacement flags
Authentication config is global by default. Use --system or --local to select another Git config scope:
setupmjr git auth --local
Use --remove when you want setupmjr to clear existing credential helpers in the selected scope before configuring the requested authentication path:
setupmjr git auth --local --remove
Do not combine --system and --local.


GitHub CLI path
On a machine where GitHub CLI credential storage works well, authenticate once:
gh auth login
setupmjr git auth
The resulting Git credential helper is the standard GitHub CLI helper. Command-line Git and tools such as R gitcreds can consume the same Git credential interface.


Headless/HPC fallback
If no persistent gh login is available, setupmjr git auth reuses, in order:

GH_TOKEN;
GITHUB_TOKEN;
an existing ~/.config/setupmjr/auth/github.token;
otherwise a token entered at the prompt.

The token is stored once with private permissions: the auth directory is mode 0700 and github.token is mode 0600 on POSIX systems. The literal token value is not copied into .gitconfig, .bashrc, .zshrc, .bashrc.d/login.sh, or .zshrc.d/login.sh.
Git is configured with a host-specific credential helper that reads the protected token file only when Git requests a credential. For shell tools that consume GH_TOKEN, setupmjr places a small non-secret managed block in ~/.bashrc.d/login.sh and ~/.zshrc.d/login.sh; those files read the same protected token file when the shell starts. .bashrc and .zshrc only source their corresponding rc.d directories.
setupmjr git auth text explicitly selects this protected-token fallback. The text name is retained for backwards compatibility with the older command.


Migration from older setupmjr authentication
Older versions of setupmjr could write GH_TOKEN directly into .bashrc.d/login.sh and .zshrc.d/login.sh. Running the current authentication setup removes active legacy GH_TOKEN= and GITHUB_USERNAME= assignments from those setupmjr login files before configuring the new strategy.
A short-lived version also placed the non-secret managed block directly in .bashrc and .zshrc. Re-running setupmjr git auth migrates that block into the existing login.sh files automatically.


Dev Containers
VS Code Dev Containers supports Git credential-helper forwarding and copies Git configuration into the container. The preferred path is therefore to configure authentication once on the HPC host with setupmjr git auth and let Dev Containers reuse that Git credential helper.
The setupmjr fallback is deliberately implemented through the standard Git credential-helper interface for this reason. If a particular remote-HPC/container combination does not forward the helper correctly, test that environment before adding container-specific secret propagation. Do not bake a PAT into devcontainer.json, a Dockerfile, an image, or a repository file.


R gitcreds
gitcreds asks Git’s credential subsystem for credentials. Both setupmjr strategies configure that same subsystem, so gitcreds::gitcreds_get("https://github.com") can use the effective GitHub credential without a separate R-specific token store.

title: git
text:
Legacy explicit helpers
The older explicit helper commands remain available but are not part of the default authentication path:
setupmjr git auth cache
setupmjr git auth mngr
